ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Bruising during treatment

A 41-year-old man taking valproate develops easy bruising and gum bleeding. He is not taking an anticoagulant and has no previous bleeding disorder. Which investigation directly assesses an important hematologic adverse effect of his medication?

  1. Serum potassium alone
  2. A fasting lipid profile alone
  3. A hearing test
  4. A sweat test
  5. Platelet count and coagulation assessment
Answer and explanation

Platelet count and coagulation assessment

Valproate can cause thrombocytopenia and impaired hemostasis; bleeding warrants evaluation.

Option explanations

Platelet count and coagulation assessment: Valproate can cause thrombocytopenia and impaired hemostasis; bleeding warrants evaluation.

Serum potassium alone: Potassium does not assess platelet number or coagulation.

A fasting lipid profile alone: Lipids do not explain this bleeding pattern.

A hearing test: This does not assess the relevant toxicity.

A sweat test: This does not evaluate acquired bleeding.
